module_title: The Birth of the Twins and the Bretton Woods Conference
introduction: In July 1944, as World War II was nearing its end, delegates from 44 nations met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire (USA), to design a new international monetary system. Their goal was to prevent another Great Depression and rebuild the shattered world economy.

core_concepts.title: Why are they called 'Twins'?
core_concepts.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank were both established at the same 1944 conference. Because they share the same 'place of birth' and the same headquarters location, they are famously known as the 'Bretton Woods Twins'.

core_concepts.title: Fundamental Difference (Short-term vs. Long-term)
core_concepts.description:
1. IMF (The Financial Doctor): It provides 'short-term' loans to help countries fix 'Balance of Payments' (BoP) crises (when a country runs out of foreign currency/dollars). 
2. World Bank (The Developer): It provides 'long-term' loans and grants for development projects like building roads, dams, schools, and hospitals to reduce poverty.

core_concepts.title: Headquarters
core_concepts.description: Both the IMF and the World Bank are headquartered in 'Washington D.C.', USA.

important_entities.name: Founding Fathers
important_entities.significance: John Maynard Keynes (UK) and Harry Dexter White (USA) were the intellectual architects who led the negotiations to create these institutions.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners often ask: 'Which of the following is NOT a Bretton Woods institution?' The answer is usually the WTO (World Trade Organization). The WTO was created much later in 1995 and is NOT a Bretton Woods twin.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Dollar crisis = IMF, Development = World Bank
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a country is 'sick' and needs an emergency dollar injection, it calls the IMF. If it wants to 'grow' its infrastructure, it calls the World Bank.

exam_strategy_tips: A direct question in SSC/Banking: 'Where are the headquarters of IMF and World Bank located?' Answer: Washington D.C.
